title: Observability ontology + quick reference cookbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact observability ontology plus a quick reference cookbook for engineers instrumenting LLM inference. Goal: reduce ambiguity between teams, speed up new instrumentation PRs, and provide ready-made widget/trace patterns for oncall and investigations.

High-level note: this is intentionally pragmatic — definitions favor operational signal usefulness over theoretical purity. Additions and edits are expected; treat this as a working cheat-sheet.

Core concepts (single-line definitions):
- request_id: immutable id for a user-facing API call; carried through routing, admission, model fan-out, and response assembly.
- session_id: higher-level grouping for multi-call user sessions (optional).
- token_path: the ordered sequence of tokens (input+generated) used to compute attention/kv cache; used for prefix-warmth and cold-start analysis.
- prefix_warmth: fraction of token_path that hits an existing KV cache at inference start. (0.0 cold, 1.0 warm)
- kvcache_hit: boolean per-model-inference call indicating whether a cache entry was reused for a prefix.
- microlatency: latency at the fine-grain op level (e.g., embed, attention kernel, kv lookup) for profiling.
- response_latency: time from API request received to first-byte to client.
- 95q_token_latency: 95th percentile per-token decode latency per model. Useful for throttles/SLOs.
- reroute_score: internal routing heuristic score that decided whether to send to a cheaper/fallback model.
- model_variant: short id for the exact model binary (includes quantization profile).
- fanout_count: how many model calls were issued for a request (multi-model pipelines).

Metric naming conventions (recommended):
- Use dot-separated names: inference.latency.response_ms, inference.kvcache.prefix_warmth_ratio, inference.embedding.dimensions, inference.cost.per_token_usd
- Tags/labels: model_variant, region, tenant_id (hashed), route, priority (low|normal|high). Keep cardinality low for on-dash tiles.
- Unit suffixes: use _ms, _ratio, _count, _usd, _tokens when helpful.

Trace/span design (span types and attributes):
- Top-level span: api.request (attrs: request_id, route, client_id_hash, method)
- Admission span: api.admit (attrs: admission_reason, priority, quota_path)
- Router span: api.route (attrs: chosen_model, reroute_score, fallback_trigger)
- Model call span: model.call (attrs: request_id, model_variant, sequence_length, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, kvcache_hit)
- Kernel spans (optional for perf builds): model.kernel.matmul, model.kernel.attention, model.kernel.kv_read
- Aggregation span: response.assemble (attrs: fanout_count, any_dedup, truncated)
- External spans: datastore.retrieval, embeddings.index_lookup, policy.evaluate

Span sampling guidance:
- Keep a low baseline sample rate (0.1%–1%) across all traffic.
- Always sample 100% of traces that hit any severity-level error or exceed critical latency (e.g., response_latency_ms > 1500).
- Spike sampling: when burst or error-rate triggers occur, increase sampling for affected tenant_id prefixes to 10% for 10m.
- For multi-model fanout requests, prefer sampling one representative model.call span fully rather than all. Use attribute representative_model=true.

Dashboard widget quick recipes (widgets you can drop into a compact incident board):
- Latency ribbon: stacked area of p50/p90/p95 token latency per model_variant (filter by route). Small and high-signal for regressions.
- Cold-start heatmap: rows = model_variant, cols = hour-of-day; cell = count of requests with prefix_warmth < 0.2. Use for capacity/caching tuning.
- KV warmth panel: time series of bucketed prefix_warmth_ratio by tenant cohort (top 10 tenants).
- Fanout matrix: matrix with source route on rows and model_variant(s) on columns, cell = average fanout_count and percent successful_first_try.
- Cost per request: per-route panel showing usd per-token * tokens_per_response_avg; annotate with percentiles.
- Re-route churn gauge: rate of reroute_score-triggered fallback decisions per minute.
- SLO burn-rate tile: rolling burn rate for response_latency_ms p95 vs SLO.

Investigation checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Is there an SLO alert? check burn-rate tile and time window.
2) Identify top-affected model_variant(s) and routes.
3) Open a sampled trace (if available) and inspect model.call spans for kernel latency spikes or kvcache misses.
4) Correlate with deployment events (GH PR/timestamp) and autoscaling events.
5) Check cold-start heatmap and KV warmth panel. If prefix_warmth dropped, consider cache eviction, padding change, or prewarming.
6) If fanout increased, check routing policy changes or upstream retries.

Instrumentation checklist for a model-serving PR (minimal required attributes):
- Attach request_id to all subsystems (router, admission, model_client).
- Emit model_variant and quant_profile as tags on model.call spans and metrics.
- Expose prefix_warmth_ratio per request as a metric (inference.kvcache.prefix_warmth).
- Emit token-level counters: input_tokens_count, output_tokens_count as metrics on request completion.
- Add boolean metric inference.model.call_retried when client retries happen.
- Add a debug-only kernel timing that flips on via feature flag (used during perf experiments only).

Sampling and cost tradeoffs (notes):
- Traces are expensive: favor high-value attributes on metrics and reduce trace span depth in steady-state.
- Use event counters for high-cardinality signals (e.g., user prompts that match certain templates) and rely on sampled traces for deep context.

Runbook snippets (copy into PagerDuty playbook):
- If p95 token latency jumps > 2x with no deploys: check kernel errors, GPU health, and rack-level telemetry; escalate to SRE.
- If prefix_warmth drops across many tenants: check cache invalidation job and redis/memstore metrics; consider temporary prewarm for high-traffic routes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define explicit tenant-hash policy for dashboards and retention. (Related: JIRA OBS-178)
- Compact representation for multi-hop traces when fanout_count > 3 (reduce trace size).
- Standardize model_variant naming to include quant bits and commit sha. (PR: GH:redwood/telemetry#412)

References and useful links:
- Telemetry repo PR: GH:redwood/telemetry#412
- Incident runbook template: confluence.redwood/infraplaybooks/obs-runbook (internal)
- Slack thread: #obs-infra (search 2023-11-07 for KV prewarm experiment)

Quick-start checklist for new engineers (30–60 min):
- Read this doc.
- Run local trace-exporter (dev instructions in telemetry repo README).
- Add a simple metric (inference.latency.response_ms) to a tiny test route and verify dashboard ingestion.
- Create a short PR with the metric and a linked GH telemetry issue.

Notes to self: keep this file compact; split off deeper sampling math into a separate ``sampling-models.md`` when we finalize burn-rate thresholds.

Last edits: trimmed widgets and added sampling guidance (2024-11-21 by Maya).
